What are HIV and AIDS?
The terms HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) and AIDS (acquired immune deficiency
syndrome) are often used synonymously. This is wrong; they do not mean the same thing. HIV is
a virus which attacks the immune system and weakens the body’s ability to fight infections. AIDS
is the final stage of HIV infection, when the body can no longer fight certain infections and
diseases such as tuberculosis (TB) or cancer.
